From 5c47251e8c4903111608ddcba2a77c0c425c247c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Herve Codina <herve.codina@bootlin.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Nov 2023 16:26:55 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] lib/vsprintf: Fix %pfwf when current node refcount == 0

A refcount issue can appeared in __fwnode_link_del() due to the
pr_debug() call:
  WARNING: CPU: 0 PID: 901 at lib/refcount.c:25 refcount_warn_saturate+0xe5/0x110
  Call Trace:
  <TASK>
  ...
  of_node_get+0x1e/0x30
  of_fwnode_get+0x28/0x40
  fwnode_full_name_string+0x34/0x90
  fwnode_string+0xdb/0x140
  ...
  vsnprintf+0x17b/0x630
  ...
  __fwnode_link_del+0x25/0xa0
  fwnode_links_purge+0x39/0xb0
  of_node_release+0xd9/0x180
  ...

Indeed, an fwnode (of_node) is being destroyed and so, of_node_release()
is called because the of_node refcount reached 0.
From of_node_release() several function calls are done and lead to
a pr_debug() calls with %pfwf to print the fwnode full name.
The issue is not present if we change %pfwf to %pfwP.

To print the full name, %pfwf iterates over the current node and its
parents and obtain/drop a reference to all nodes involved.

In order to allow to print the full name (%pfwf) of a node while it is
being destroyed, do not obtain/drop a reference to this current node.

Fixes: a92eb7621b9f ("lib/vsprintf: Make use of fwnode API to obtain node names and separators")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Herve Codina <herve.codina@bootlin.com>
Reviewed-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Petr Mladek <pmladek@suse.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20231114152655.409331-1-herve.codina@bootlin.com

diff --git a/lib/vsprintf.c b/lib/vsprintf.c
index 3e3733a7084f..552738f14275 100644
--- a/lib/vsprintf.c
+++ b/lib/vsprintf.c
@@ -2111,15 +2111,20 @@ char *fwnode_full_name_string(struct fwnode_handle *fwnode, char *buf,
 
 	/* Loop starting from the root node to the current node. */
 	for (depth = fwnode_count_parents(fwnode); depth >= 0; depth--) {
-		struct fwnode_handle *__fwnode =
-			fwnode_get_nth_parent(fwnode, depth);
+		/*
+		 * Only get a reference for other nodes (i.e. parent nodes).
+		 * fwnode refcount may be 0 here.
+		 */
+		struct fwnode_handle *__fwnode = depth ?
+			fwnode_get_nth_parent(fwnode, depth) : fwnode;
 
 		buf = string(buf, end, fwnode_get_name_prefix(__fwnode),
 			     default_str_spec);
 		buf = string(buf, end, fwnode_get_name(__fwnode),
 			     default_str_spec);
 
-		fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode);
+		if (depth)
+			fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode);
 	}
 
 	return buf;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `lib/vsprintf.c`**
- The loop that iterates over the current node and its parents has been modified to avoid obtaining a reference for the current node when its depth is 0. 
- The line that previously obtained a reference for the current node (`fwnode_get_nth_parent(fwnode, depth)`) has been replaced with a conditional statement that assigns the current node directly to `__fwnode` when `depth` is 0.
- The call to `fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode)` has been made conditional, so it is only called if `depth` is not 0.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The changes made in `lib/vsprintf.c` are directly related to fixing a refcount issue that occurs when the current node is being destroyed. By preventing the reference count from being altered for the current node during its destruction (when `depth` is 0), the patch addresses the warning that arises from the `pr_debug()` call in the `of_node_release()` function. This modification ensures that the full name of the fwnode can still be printed without causing a refcount saturation warning, thus maintaining the integrity of the reference counting mechanism while allowing for proper logging.

Indeed, an fwnode (of_node) is being destroyed and so, of_node_release()
is called because the of_node refcount reached 0.
From of_node_release() several function calls are done and lead to
a pr_debug() calls with %pfwf to print the fwnode full name.
The issue is not present if we change %pfwf to %pfwP.

To print the full name, %pfwf iterates over the current node and its

Fixes: a92eb7621b9f ("lib/vsprintf: Make use of fwnode API to obtain node names and separators")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Herve Codina <herve.codina@bootlin.com>
Reviewed-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20231114152655.409331-1-herve.codina@bootlin.com

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by a refcount issue that occurs when the `pr_debug()` call attempts to print the full name of an fwnode while it is being destroyed. Specifically, the function `fwnode_full_name_string` iterates over the current node and its parents, obtaining and dropping references to these nodes. When the current node's reference count reaches 0, it leads to a warning due to the attempt to access it, resulting in a refcount saturation warning.

Here is the patch:
 
 static noinline_for_stack
 char *fwnode_full_name_string(struct fwnode_handle *fwnode, char *buf,
 			      char *end)
 {
 	int depth;
 
 	/* Loop starting from the root node to the current node. */
 	for (depth = fwnode_count_parents(fwnode); depth >= 0; depth--) {
-		struct fwnode_handle *__fwnode =
-			fwnode_get_nth_parent(fwnode, depth);
+		/*
+		 * Only get a reference for other nodes (i.e. parent nodes).
+		 * fwnode refcount may be 0 here.
+		 */
+		struct fwnode_handle *__fwnode = depth ?
+			fwnode_get_nth_parent(fwnode, depth) : fwnode;
 
 		buf = string(buf, end, fwnode_get_name_prefix(__fwnode),
 			     default_str_spec);
 		buf = string(buf, end, fwnode_get_name(__fwnode),
 			     default_str_spec);
 
-		fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode);
+		if (depth)
+			fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode);
 	}
 
 	return buf;
 }

```c

fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `fwnode_full_name_string` function attempts to obtain a reference to the current node (fwnode) while it is being destroyed, leading to a situation where the reference count can reach 0. This results in a warning when the `pr_debug()` call tries to access the fwnode, which is no longer valid.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
struct fwnode_handle *__fwnode = depth ? fwnode_get_nth_parent(fwnode, depth) : fwnode;
if (depth) fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode);
```
Reason:
The fix modifies the logic to avoid obtaining a reference for the current node when it is being destroyed. Instead, it only obtains references for parent nodes, thus preventing the refcount issue and allowing the full name to be printed safely without causing a saturation warning.
